profiled_workloads.selection_reason: lowest eval speedup of the round (0.2962) and representative of the three small 1x16x64x64->128x128 fixtures
highest eval latency of the round (0.6316 ms) and representative of the three large 4x32x128x128->256x256 fixtures (2-byte dtype)

findings.label: Per-program fixed cost dominates device scaling: 512-element programs cost 3.23 us/program while 2048-element programs cost only 6.15 us/program
findings.backend_detail: msprof aiv_time/aiv_scalar_time consistently track the fitted fixed share (aiv_scalar_time 17.66 us small, 216.32 us large).
findings.inference: Row geometry from the source: timing-4 uses BR=8, IWP=64 (512 input elements per program, 256 programs) and timing-3 uses BR=16, IWP=128 (2048 input elements per program, 2048 programs); both match the Block Num column exactly. Dividing kernel time by programs/20 cores gives 3.23 us (small) and 6.15 us (large) per program, i.e. a 4x increase in tile elements yields only 1.9x more per-program time. A two-point linear fit is ~2.24 us fixed + ~1.9 ns per input element per program, which attributes roughly 29/41 us of the small kernel and 229/630 us of the large kernel to per-program cost. The dtype differs between the two fixtures (fp32 vs bf16), which weakens the fit, so this is an inference rather than a decomposition.

findings.label: Large fixture is device-bound and vector-pipeline dominated; contiguous stores are cheap and the row-gather loads are secondary
findings.backend_detail: Ratios are marginal pipeline-active statistics and are not added into a time decomposition; vec+scalar happens to be close to the kernel duration (631.7 us vs 629.8 us) in this sample, which is treated only as a lead.
findings.inference: The eval latency for this fixture (0.6316 ms) equals the profiled kernel duration (0.6298 ms), so this regime is device-bound. The contiguous join/store path costs only 8.2 us of MTE3 while the vector stage is 415 us, and the two row-gather loads cost 179 us of MTE2, so the interpolation arithmetic and index handling on fp32 tiles (vertical blend, two tl.gather calls, even/odd blend, join, dtype convert) are the element-proportional cost, not the output write. Logical traffic is about 16.8 MB read + 16.8 MB written in 630 us, so this kernel is far from a bandwidth limit; no Roofline claim is made.

findings.label: Small fixtures still spend more than half of eval latency outside the device kernel, even though the kernel itself is also inefficient
findings.backend_detail: One kernel per call (operation_count=1); no extra cast/TransData stages in the candidate path.
findings.inference: Eval latency for this fixture is 0.1024 ms while the single profiled device kernel is 41.42 us, so roughly 60 us of each call is outside the kernel (allocation plus Python/JIT dispatch in run()); the profiler run itself inflates host gaps, so this is a qualitative split from two independent collections, not a subtraction-validated decomposition. Round 3 already removed 23.9-29.9% of the small-case latency by caching metadata-derived launch parameters, which confirms the host path is a real and still large contributor. Separately, the 41.4 us kernel is about 3.3x the vendor ResizeBilinearV2 stage seen for the same geometry in the round-2 paired reference trace, so host-only work cannot reach the 0.8x target: this kernel's device time alone exceeds the reference total (30.3 us).

performance_interpretation: Round 3 raised geo_mean from 0.3033 to 0.3450 (geo_mean_delta_pct 13.73). All of the gain came from the three small fixtures (latency -23.9% to -29.9%), which is consistent with the launch-parameter cache removing host work; the three large fixtures moved by less than 0.2% and remain device-bound (timing-3: 0.6298 ms kernel vs 0.6316 ms eval). The frozen hypothesis (small fixtures dominated by per-call Python parameter derivation) is therefore supported for the host part but incomplete: after the cache, ~60 us of host time per small call remains, and the small kernel itself (41.4 us) is still ~3.3x the vendor resize stage. Both regimes show a large aiv_scalar share (0.43 small, 0.34 large) and a program-count/tile-size relation that implies a per-program fixed cost of roughly 2.2 us, so the next lever is device-side amortization, not further parameter derivation.

next_experiment.action_description: In the fast-path host resolution only (_UB_ELEMS and _pick_rows_per_program), raise the per-program tile so BR covers ~4096 input columns instead of 512 (small fixtures: BR 8 -> 32) and avoids the _TARGET_PROGRAMS=256 cap forcing small tiles; keep the kernel body, the fp32 interpolation math, masking and the general flat path unchanged, and compile-check the resulting UB footprint per dtype before committing (fp16 first, then bf16/fp32, with multibuffer left at the default so the failure mode is observable in the compile log rather than silently re-tuned).
next_experiment.expected_impact: Program count should fall from 2048 to ~512 (large) and from 256 to ~64 (small). If the per-program fixed cost hypothesis holds, aiv_scalar_time should drop from 216 us toward ~60-115 us and from 17.7 us toward ~7 us, with kernel time falling ~20-35% on the large fixtures and ~30-50% of the device portion on the small ones. A host-only view of the small fixtures would then be roughly 20-25 us device + ~60 us host, so their eval latency can only approach 0.8x once the host path is also reduced in a later round.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: UB overflow is the concrete risk: the fast path holds v, vm, vp, even, odd and the joined (BR, IWP, 2) tile in fp32, so a 4x tile may exceed the 192 KiB UB for fp32 even if fp16 compiles (the SELU 16384-block failure is the precedent). It may also lose load balance when n_rows is not a multiple of the larger BR (tail masking is already present but the last wave may be partial). Rollback is to restore the round-3 _UB_ELEMS/_pick_rows_per_program values; no semantics change is intended, so any numerical or layout regression also means revert.
success_criteria: Full KGS correctness still 18/18 with the frozen tolerances (including the 1x1 outputs and both align_corners settings), and the 48-case semantic gate does not regress.
Headline geo_mean exceeds the round-3 value 0.344965 with per-case latencies recorded, and both a small and a large candidate latency drop in the same run.

A re-profiled workload shows the predicted metric movement: Block Num down ~4x and aiv_scalar_time down proportionally; if program count falls but aiv_scalar_time and kernel time do not, the per-program-cost hypothesis is falsified and the next check is whether tl.gather scalarizes (instruction listing was cancelled this round).
